llm.summary: This news skill mostly aggregates public feeds, but it should be reviewed because it mixes removed monitoring and push features with active-looking persistence, cron, and optional long-running service instructions.

dimensions.detail: Network access to many public news and social sources is purpose-aligned, though the scope is broad and includes optional deep fetching with Playwright and X/Twitter access requiring cookies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package inspected is a Markdown-only skill with no bundled executable code, but it includes optional pip installs, git clone instructions, and Docker self-deployment commands for external services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The file says the TrendRadar monitoring and push engine was removed, but later sections still describe keyword tracking, smart push rules, source health monitoring, cron schedules, and TrendRadar-derived reporting as if they may be active.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses local workspace archives, 30-day retention, permanent retention for high-heat events, daily cleanup, optional push channels, cron timing, and Docker containers with restart behavior; user control is mentioned but the active boundary is not fully consistent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is broad news aggregation, sentiment analysis, and report generation from public APIs, RSS feeds, search, and social hot lists; that is coherent with most listed capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with broad public-source fetching and local news archives. Do not enable push channels, cron schedules, X/Twitter cookies, Playwright deep fetching, or Docker self-hosting unless you explicitly want those behaviors and can review the configuration.
llm.findings:
[P2] expected: The flagged hidden-instruction evidence is an ordinary HTML/RSS template comment, not an instruction to override the agent or perform unauthorized actions.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-focused sentiment analysis and Chinese report templates are consistent with the skill’s presentation; this is a locale limitation rather than a security concern.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The concern is supported in part: monitoring, push, keyword tracking, cron, and retention content remains after the file says the monitoring/push engine was removed, creating real scope ambiguity.
[RP1] expected: The Docker commands are optional self-hosting instructions and use explicit version tags, but not immutable digests; users should treat them as supply-chain and persistence decisions.
